name: design-doc-drafter
description: Turns requirements you paste into the chat into a software design document with a fixed structure: context and goals, a requirements table with ids (R1, R2...), components, contracts, data flow, data model, failure modes, security, observability, rollout, acceptance criteria per requirement, alternatives and open questions. Requirement ids, vague-word detection, coverage and section order are computed in code; the model proposes the design. It never invents numbers: an unknown scale, latency or budget becomes a visible [TBD] and an open question, and technologies you didn't name are labelled "Proposed" with the requirement they serve. Answer an open question ("Q2: 500 requests/second") and only the affected sections update. ADR style on request; an agent-design appendix for LLM or agent systems. It drafts only and writes nothing anywhere. Not for writing or reviewing code, project plans or general questions.

skills.name: Draft a design document
skills.description: A design document from pasted requirements: ids, components, contracts, data flow, failure modes, acceptance criteria and open questions, with unknown numbers marked [TBD]. Draft only.
examples: Draft a design doc for these requirements: <paste the requirements>
ADR for choosing a queue given these constraints: <paste the constraints>
